response.markdown_report:
Select a **candidate-distribution stress audit** of the existing NextItNet before changing its architecture. At 0% progress, this offers a small, measurable extension of the supplied diagnostic adapter.

**Insights from the starting point.**

1. Recent-history deletion reduces margins more than older-history deletion in all four categories. This establishes sensitivity, but does not support the qualitative claim that older interests dominate recommendations.
2. Sampled negative-win rates are only 2.60–6.38%. These training-pair measurements leave competition among plausible top-ranked alternatives unresolved.
3. Sampled causality and in-memory scoring checks pass. Generated-predictor reload parity remains unverified, so deployment correctness needs a separate check.

**Insights from related work.**

1. Sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons [1]. Comparing candidate distributions can expose limitations of an apparently healthy pairwise margin.
2. Hard negatives can be unobserved positives [2]. Semantic neighbors should therefore be treated as ambiguous competitors rather than confirmed preference errors.
3. NextItNet provides a causal convolutional backbone with bounded temporal dependencies [3]. Candidate auditing can reuse its unchanged features and scoring interfaces without introducing another predictor.

These insights suggest three directions: candidate competition, temporal mechanism testing, and feedback grounding.

| Direction | Existing evidence | Next measurement | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Competition | Healthy sampled pairs | Uniform/frequency/lexical candidate ranks | Generalization |
| Temporal mechanism | Recent-deletion sensitivity | Controlled residual interventions | Causal interpretation |
| Feedback grounding | Aggregate qualitative diagnosis | Evidence-linked rejection annotation | Unobserved intent and compatibility |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate stress audit [1,2] | 4/7/4 | Originality: useful integration, established components. Potential: reveals hidden competition, training memorization limits conclusions. Difficulty: reuses scoring, requires careful candidate bookkeeping. |
| Residual-branch fault calibration [3] | 5/6/6 | Originality: family-specific adaptation, established intervention method. Potential: localizes defects, artificial faults may mislead. Difficulty: accessible hooks, alignment and controls require care. |
| Feedback evidence ledger | 3/6/3 | Originality: disciplined task adaptation, standard annotation. Potential: separates unknowns from mismatch, only twenty users support it. Difficulty: simple schema, actual feedback records and adjudication required. |

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze training-only prefix–next-item examples and reuse each across three equally sized, unique distractor sets: uniform, training-frequency weighted, and title/description TF-IDF neighbors. Exclude padding, the target and prefix items; record later-training positives as conflicts. For a bounded subset, score the eligible catalog in chunks and compare sampled ranks with exact ranks using explicit tie handling.

Report support, metadata coverage, fallback counts, rank quantiles and sampled/full-catalog hit disagreement by prefix length and training-frequency band. Label every result a training diagnostic; preserve pinned macro validation HR@10 as the sole selection criterion. Preserve one NextItNet checkpoint per category and verify generated-predictor parity separately. No accuracy improvement is established by the supplied evidence.

idea.description: Extend the family-aware DiagnosisProbe with a frozen, training-only candidate-distribution stress audit. Score identical prefix–target examples against uniform, frequency-weighted and lexical distractors using the same trained NextItNet, then measure sampled/full-catalog ranking disagreement on a bounded subset.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics establish healthy sampled-pair separation and stronger recent-history sensitivity, but cannot establish top-list specificity or benchmark HR@10. Candidate stress testing directly examines whether easy sampled negatives conceal competition from plausible alternatives, without assuming unobserved intent, satisfied needs or compatibility.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView interfaces. Retain existing metrics and definitions. Obtain stable diagnostic example identifiers from permitted user_train histories; loader rows alone do not identify users. Use only supplied training interactions and permitted titles/descriptions; ignore unavailable review, rating and item-category fields. Fit TF-IDF locally without pretrained weights. Freeze bounded example selection, candidate IDs, local seed 42, sampling weights, exclusions, tie policy and fallback rules. Use at most 99 unique distractors per sampler, requiring the same feasible size across samplers for each example. Report insufficient support explicitly. Exclude prefix items and target; identify distractors that occur later in that user's available training history as known-positive conflicts, without treating other unobserved items as true negatives. Report raw and conflict-filtered comparisons with their different denominators. Select each sequence's largest nonzero index, exclude all-padding sequences, and retain original targets throughout. For catalog diagnostics, exclude padding and prefix items while retaining the target; chunk scores to bound GPU memory. Use the host tie policy when available, otherwise document a diagnostic policy without claiming benchmark equivalence. Preserve and restore module modes in finally, use no_grad, and keep all audit artifacts trial-local. Empty measurements return null with zero support. The interpreter must distinguish training diagnostics, sensitivity, qualitative feedback and independent validation. Keep all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, and 200 batches per epoch unchanged. Load one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category, with no score fusion or checkpoint averaging. This diagnostic extension requires no architecture change; separately verify the existing generated predictor against the trained model on identical mapped histories and candidates. Bound audit inference within the shared search budget.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        previous_mode = self.view.model.training
        self.view.model.eval()
        try:
            with torch.no_grad():
                metrics, definitions = existing_family_specific_probes(train_loader)
                examples = freeze_bounded_training_prefixes(self.view.user_train, seed=42)
                lexical_index = fit_tfidf_on_permitted_titles_and_descriptions()
                for example in examples:
                    sequence, target, prefix_items, later_training_items = example
                    t = largest_nonzero_index(sequence)
                    if t is None:
                        record_exclusion('all_padding')
                        continue
                    features = self.view.log2feats(sequence)[t]
                    eligible = catalog_without_padding_target_or_prefix(example)
                    candidates = freeze_equal_size_unique_candidate_sets(
                        eligible, samplers=['uniform', 'training_frequency', 'tfidf'],
                        maximum_negatives=99, seed=42)
                    for sampler, negatives in candidates.items():
                        scores = self.view.predict_score(features, [target] + negatives)
                        record_rank_and_margin_with_support(scores, sampler)
                        record_known_positive_conflicts(negatives, later_training_items)
                    if example_is_in_fixed_catalog_subset(example):
                        exact_rank = rank_target_by_chunked_catalog_scoring(
                            features, target, exclude=prefix_items, tie_policy=recorded_policy)
                        record_sampled_catalog_disagreement(exact_rank, candidates)
                return {
                    'metrics': merge_supported_training_diagnostics(metrics),
                    'metric_definitions': merge_definitions_and_limits(definitions)
                }
        finally:
            self.view.model.train(previous_mode)

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return build_prompt(raw_diagnosis,
        require_support_and_definition_grounding=True,
        label_training_memorization_and_false_negative_ambiguity=True,
        forbid_inferring_validation_HR_or_unobserved_user_needs=True)

# Host execution separately checks generated-predictor reload parity.
# Model selection remains the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Combines candidate-distribution stress tests and exact-rank calibration within the supplied family-aware diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Sampling audits, TF-IDF retrieval and exact ranking are established techniques; the contribution is their controlled integration.

future_potential.positive: Can reveal whether apparently healthy training margins conceal difficult candidate competition and guide a subsequent single-model loss intervention.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix results may reflect memorization, and semantic competition does not establish actual user preference or validation improvement.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses frozen NextItNet features and scores without fitting an auxiliary recommendation model or changing inference architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Unique sampling, sparse metadata, conflict tracking, exact-rank ties and bounded catalog scoring require careful bookkeeping.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can yield conclusions inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
Motivates comparing sampled target ranks with exact catalog ranks.
limitations: Does not establish a defect in the supplied NextItNet.
Does not justify changing the pinned benchmark evaluator.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: Examines false-negative risk associated with difficult unobserved items.
Motivates distinguishing known-positive conflicts from ambiguous unobserved competitors.
limitations: Does not provide true negative labels for this task.
Its training approach requires separate matched evaluation before adoption.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Introduces causal dilated convolutional modeling for next-item recommendation.
Provides the backbone retained by the proposed diagnostic audit.
limitations: Architecture alone does not establish current user intent or practical item compatibility.
Published results do not establish performance under the supplied RecHarness splits and evaluator.
